_about: The `bayn showcase` tour: simulated EEG + these recordings (a team member reading the fictional corpus scripts, tests/data/corpus.json, through the wireless demo mic). Times in seconds. trigger_at_s is relative to the start of the scene's audio (negative = before it: the seizure clip needs EEG lead time). after_s = silence after the audio, so each event's window (-10/+30 s) holds only its own scene.

scenes.title: Jaw clench · Arabic
scenes.caption: A teacher describes a pupil's episode in Arabic and clenches their jaw to mark it. Bayn saves the EEG from 10 s before to 30 s after, transcribes what was said and writes a summary.

scenes.title: Button · English
scenes.caption: No gesture needed: the Trigger button (or the T key) does exactly the same.

scenes.title: Triple blink · Arabic with English terms
scenes.caption: Three firm blinks trigger it hands-free. The speech mixes Arabic with English terms, and each utterance is transcribed in its own language.

scenes.title: Seizure socket · mock model
scenes.caption: Nobody triggers this one. A replayed hospital EEG clip (CHB-MIT) contains a seizure, and the mock model in the detector socket flags it while the lesson goes on. Not validated on Muse data, not a diagnosis.
